# Isolated TLS reference diagnostic

Manual-only replacement of the already registered `.github/workflows/diagnose-canva.yml` (workflow ID 410610164) on `diagnostics/canva-font-validation-rc78`. No normal branch, release, deployment, schedule, or pull-request trigger. Parent branch snapshot: 85b6f3335e89aad33d057b2f75e6a1a7ca50494b. The full existing workflow graph was checked: downstream release/site jobs listen to other workflow names and dev/main branches.

This performs at most one public Canva proof using published abx-plugins 1.13.655, abx-dl 1.13.320, official TLSNotary extension 0.1.0.1501, its published export2/mux1 overlays, Chrome 156.0.8078.47, Node 24.22.1, and the immutable alpha.15 verifier image. Source/download/lock hashes are in pins.json. The gateway is built only from allowlisted wheel files with its original locked dependencies and pinned official Node base. This is a source-pinned reference, not evidence of deployed-server equivalence. The earlier local Docker Desktop attempts never started a proof and are not retried or repaired here.

Fresh native AMD64 Ubuntu runs the stock Chrome sandbox. If a trusted installed root-owned sandbox helper is available, its package ownership, mode, and package checksum are verified before use. No helper installation, chmod, chown, sysctl, AppArmor change, privileged containers, or sandbox bypass is permitted. A disposable browser preflight must report adequate sandboxing before services or proof start. Failure stops the attempt.

The original proof deadlines, request sizes, admission checks, container memory/CPU/PID limits, no-new-privileges, and capability drops are preserved. Gateway is localhost-only; verifier uses an internal network. No credentials, provider secrets, or real profiles enter child environments. The signing key is generated only for the owned ephemeral fixture and is deleted, along with receipts, transcripts, profiles, and private diagnostic logs. Verifier logs are never read. Receipt verification and all five tamper-rejection checks run locally on success.

Only schema-validated summary.json may be uploaded: source hashes, versions, fixed startup error classifications (never arbitrary stderr), transport enums/counters, cgroup memory counters, container outcome fields, and cleanup booleans. It excludes keys, payloads, headers, URLs, receipts, transcripts, process/session identifiers. A failed proof, missing evidence, or uncertain teardown fails the workflow. There are no proof retries or increased limits.

Offline contract tests run before execution. A private, durable ownership journal supports an always-run external cleanup step after the harness, including interrupted execution; it is never uploaded. Missing cgroup or lifecycle evidence cannot count as diagnostic success, even when receipt verification succeeds. Exact prepared extension hashes are recorded after stable post-overlay completion. Sandbox/package/platform differences remain explicit limits; a reference success cannot establish production equivalence, and a failure alone is not sufficient to select an upstream backport.

## Prior native downloader baseline

Python is pinned to 3.13.18, observed in run 42450906708, job 128639735285 (the successful setup before the TLS failure). The 28-package default abx-dl 1.13.320 / abx-plugins 1.13.655 closure is projected offline from commit 85b6f3335e89aad33d057b2f75e6a1a7ca50494b's uv.lock. All versions and allowed official wheel hashes come exclusively from that file. No dependency resolution, artifact fetch, or install was used to derive it. The selected closure has no conditional dependency edges or package forks; unfamiliar marker/extra edges fail validation rather than being guessed. Optional extras and ArchiveBox development dependencies are not selected.

This matches the prior downloader closure, not the full prior ArchiveBox environment. Node, Chrome, extension, verifier, security settings, resource limits and proof behavior remain unchanged. Run derive_requirements.py to verify the committed requirements against the source lock. Setup/proof on native Linux remain unvalidated; offline checks do not establish artifact availability.
